html:
Surinam was a plantation colony on the northeast coast of South America, in what is now Suriname. The map shows it in 1650 and 1700.

English planters from Barbados settled it in 1650 under Lord Willoughby. In 1667 a fleet from the Dutch province of Zeeland took it. In the Treaty of Breda that year the Dutch kept Surinam and the English kept New Amsterdam, which became New York.

Under the Dutch it became one of the richest and harshest sugar colonies in the Americas, worked by enslaved Africans from the Atlantic slave trade. Many escaped into the rainforest and formed free Maroon peoples, such as the Saramaka and Ndyuka, who fought the colony until it signed peace treaties with them in the 1760s.

The colony stayed Dutch for three centuries, later as Dutch Guiana, until independence in 1975.
